analysis.one_liner: Bharti Airtel is India's second-largest telecom operator by subscribers, running mobile, broadband, DTH and enterprise/digital services across India and Africa, with majority stakes in tower company Indus Towers and data-centre arm Nxtra.
tags: Jio Platforms now bigger by m-cap
analysis.whats_happening: Airtel reported Q2 FY27 (quarter ended September 2026) results on 4 November 2026: consolidated revenue of ₹60,878 crore (+16.7% YoY) and EBITDA of ₹34,946 crore, with India mobile ARPU rising to ₹271 from ₹256 a year earlier. Reported net profit of about ₹8,888 crore is being described as both a 9% and a 31% YoY rise across different outlets - the gap comes from exceptional items in last year's base, so the headline growth percentage is not strictly comparable. Separately, newly-listed Jio Platforms overtook Airtel in market capitalisation ($137.2bn vs $127.8bn), and Airtel stock dipped around 2.7% on that listing news days before its own results.
analysis.plain_terms: Airtel is the steadier of India's two healthy telecom players, raising prices (ARPU) faster than it is losing customers, which is why profit and cash flow keep climbing. But the stock trades at roughly 40-45 times earnings - a rich price that assumes tariff hikes keep coming. The tension: a newly listed Jio Platforms is now worth more by market value, and Airtel's own profit-growth number this quarter is distorted by one-off items last year, so don't take the flashier percentage at face value.
analysis.quarters: Revenue and EBITDA growth have been consistent and genuine - EBITDA margin held near 57% this quarter versus ₹33,303 crore last quarter. ARPU has climbed steadily (₹256 to ₹271 YoY), which management has long said needs to reach ₹300 for a 'respectable return on capital employed.' The net profit YoY figure varies sharply by source (9% vs 31%) because of exceptional items in the year-ago quarter - the EBITDA and ARPU trends are the more reliable read on underlying performance, not the PAT growth headline.
analysis.performance_read: The stock has returned 129.7% over 3 years and 204.8% over 5 years, well ahead of the Nifty (28.8% and 38.3%) and far ahead of Vodafone Idea over those periods. Over the last year, though, it is up only 4.55% while Vodafone Idea rallied 34.84% - that's a low-base speculative bounce in the peer, not a sign Airtel is underperforming structurally. The stock is only 2.4% off its all-time high and not near its 52-week low. The one 2:1 split (2009) is already baked into the price series shown; there is no demerger or spin-off distorting these returns.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E estimates range roughly 40-45x across sources, a steep premium to the telecom sector median (~24x). That premium exists because Airtel is seen as the highest-quality, lowest-risk operator in a two-and-a-half-player Indian telecom market with pricing power - the peer median is dragged down by a financially stressed Vodafone Idea, making the 'median' comparison somewhat misleading. Whether that premium is justified depends on whether ARPU keeps rising toward ₹300; it is expensive on every conventional earnings multiple, not cheap.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is now both volume and price-led: India revenue rose 9.4% YoY on a mix of ARPU hikes and a growing broadband/enterprise base, while EBITDA margin has stayed broadly flat near 57% rather than expanding sharply - this points to durable, not purely accounting-driven, growth. The Nxtra data-centre buildout (targeting 1 GW capacity in two years) is a newer, capital-intensive growth leg layered on top of the core telecom business.
analysis.health_read: Cash conversion looks strong - operating cash flow hit a record ₹1,22,230 crore in FY26, and net debt (ex-leases) has fallen to roughly ₹91,000 crore with net debt/EBITDA down to 0.84x, down from higher levels in recent years. Debt/equity near 1.0x is still meaningful, so financial risk is moderate rather than negligible, but the bigger watch item is business risk - competitive intensity from Jio Platforms' newly listed scale and any regulatory/AGR-related liabilities, which were not independently verified here.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding (the Mittal family plus Singtel as the foreign promoter) has risen from about 48.87% to roughly 50% in the September 2026 quarter, with zero promoter pledging reported - a clean, improving ownership signal. Note: FII/institutional percentages across different trackers did not reconcile with each other in this search (one source showed FII near 13%, another near 25%), so treat the exact institutional split as not verified - check Screener or the company's official shareholding filing for the precise breakdown. No single marquee outside investor stands out on the register beyond Singtel as the long-standing foreign promoter.
strengths: ARPU rose to ₹271 from ₹256 YoY (+5.9%), moving toward management's stated ₹300 threshold for healthy capital returns
EBITDA margin held near 57% with EBITDA of ₹34,946 crore in the quarter, showing growth isn't just a pricing mirage
Record operating cash flow of ₹1,22,230 crore in FY26 funded deleveraging to a 0.84x net debt/EBITDA ratio
Promoter stake increased to ~50% with zero pledging, signalling promoter confidence
watchpoints: P/E near 40-45x prices in continued tariff hikes; any pause in ARPU increases would hit the valuation hard
Jio Platforms' listing pushed its market cap ($137.2bn) above Airtel's ($127.8bn), resetting competitive and valuation comparisons in the sector

Reported net profit growth for the latest quarter is quoted as both 9% and 31% YoY across sources due to exceptional items in the base quarter - the headline PAT growth figure is not strictly comparable

Debt/equity still near 1.0x and heavy ongoing capex (5G, Nxtra data centres) will keep depreciation and interest costs elevated; AGR dues and other contingent liabilities were not verified in this review
analysis.one_thing: Whether India ARPU keeps climbing toward management's ₹300 target via further tariff hikes without meaningful subscriber loss to Jio - watch the Q3 FY27 ARPU and net-subscriber-addition numbers.
analysis.data_notes: Revenue, EBITDA and ARPU figures for Q2 FY27 were cross-checked across Upstox, BusinessToday, Kotak Neo and Social News XYZ and were consistent. P/E, net debt and promoter/institutional shareholding percentages varied meaningfully across sources (e.g., FII holding cited as both ~13% and ~25%); these are flagged as unreconciled rather than averaged. AGR dues and other regulatory contingent liabilities were not verified - check the company's latest annual report or Screener for confirmation.
